title: 1066: The Norman Conquest
summary: Three claimants, two invasions and the battle that changed England: from the Norwegian landing in Yorkshire to William's coronation on Christmas Day.

events.title: Battle of Fulford
events.text: The Norwegians defeat the northern earls outside York.

events.title: Battle of Stamford Bridge
events.text: After a forced march north, Harold surprises and destroys the Norwegian army. Harald Hardrada is killed.

events.title: Normans land at Pevensey
events.text: Three days after Stamford Bridge, William lands unopposed on the south coast.

events.title: Battle of Hastings
events.text: A day-long battle on Senlac Hill. The Norman cavalry's feigned retreats break the English shield wall; King Harold is killed.

events.title: Submission at Berkhamsted
events.text: The English leaders submit to William.

events.title: William crowned at Westminster
events.text: William the Conqueror is crowned King of England on Christmas Day.

story.title: A kingdom with three claimants
story.text: In January 1066 King Edward the Confessor died without children. **Harold Godwinson** was crowned king, but two powerful rivals claimed the throne: **Harald Hardrada**, King of Norway, and **William, Duke of Normandy**.

story.title: The Norwegians land in the north
story.text: Harald Hardrada sailed with around 300 ships, landed near York and beat the northern English earls at **Fulford** on 20 September.

story.title: Stamford Bridge
story.text: Harold marched his army about 300 km north in just a few days and took the Norwegians by surprise at **Stamford Bridge**. Hardrada was killed and the invasion collapsed.

story.title: William lands in the south
story.text: Only three days later, William's fleet crossed the Channel and landed at **Pevensey**. Harold had to rush his tired army all the way back south.

story.title: The Battle of Hastings
story.text: On 14 October the armies met on Senlac Hill. The English shield wall held for hours, but Norman **feigned retreats** drew men out of line. By evening Harold was dead and the English army broke.

story.title: The road to the crown
story.text: William secured Dover and Canterbury, circled around London and crossed the Thames at Wallingford. The English leaders submitted at Berkhamsted, and William was crowned in **Westminster Abbey on Christmas Day 1066**.
